edges.description: Active Gs-alpha stimulates adenylyl cyclase and increases cAMP production.
Increased cAMP availability activates the shared somatotroph cAMP/PKA module.
cAMP/PKA signaling drives excess GH secretion.
cAMP-responsive somatotroph cells proliferate in the presence of oncogenic Gs-alpha signaling.

nodes.description: Active Gs-alpha increases adenylyl cyclase activity and intracellular cAMP levels in GH-secreting pituitary tumor cells.

evidence.reference_title: GTPase-inhibiting mutations activate the alpha-chain of Gs in human tumours.
evidence.snippet: A subset of human growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary tumours, characterized by elevated GH secretion, cyclic AMP levels, and adenylyl cyclase activity, carries mutations in the gene that encodes the alpha-chain of Gs.
